BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.

IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's SPA Draft and Disclosure Letter

**Status:** Internal analysis for the Wattlebridge deal team. Not legal advice to the Seller. Terms should be confirmed by NSW counsel before mark-up.

## 1. Preliminary points

- **The Seller's "FINAL" labels, "settled at principal level" claim, and "market standard" preamble do not bind us.** Under playbook sections 0.4 and 6.3, none of these makes a position agreed or cleared. We should say so expressly in the cover note so the Seller cannot later argue we accepted them.
- **Several Seller numbers match our fallbacks, but that does not clear them.** The 20% / AUD 4.8M cap is a conditional fallback that requires prior written authority from Amelia Frost, identifying the draft. None has been given. The 18-month claims period also needs her written approval.
- **The facts are stale.** The disclosure letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. Before mark-up we should refresh the Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonus, DD-006 and Sandbar positions. Any figure in the Seller's letter should be treated as an assertion until we verify it.

## 2. Departures from playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Departure |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8M | Start 25% / AUD 6.0M; 20% only with Frost authority | Opens below our start point; fallback offered without authority |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x higher; many small claims excluded |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | First AUD 250k of losses irrecoverable; a deductible, not a tipping basket |
| General claims period (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with Frost approval) | Shortened without approval |
| Fundamental/Title (cl 12) | Same caps and time limits as general | 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | Fundamental regime removed entirely |
| Limitations/reliance (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5) | Apply to all Claims of any nature | Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct carved out to max extent enforceable | No fraud carve-out; non-reliance could shield deliberate misconduct |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room, accounts, statutory registers, public records | Specific fair disclosure only; reject deemed data-room/register disclosure | Blanket disclosure would neutralise warranty claims |
| Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3) | No claim for anything known to Buyer/advisers, including data-room or public-record matters | Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Constructive-knowledge bar; the Seller's own letter makes the data room a moving target |
| Bluefen (cl 3/6.3; DL 2) | Reasonable endeavours; consent "satisfied on delivery" of counterparty consent; no final consent in data room | Effective consent AND evidence of conditions satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient | Consent-on-delivery; conditions not required to be met |
| Riverlark (cl 2/7; DL 3) | ~AUD 3.2M outstanding; release "following Completion"; not repaid | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval | Security stays in place after Completion; no payout mechanic |
| Bonuses (funds flow; DL 5) | AUD 420k "a matter for the Seller", not in funds flow; on-costs unstated | Specific line item or seller-funded, including triggered on-costs; funds flow must not silently exclude | Flow omits the amount; on-costs unquantified |
| Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure; AUD 180k not independently verified | Narrow indemnity; no bank verification of non-payment or assignment |
| DD-006 export incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way | We should not accept the materiality conclusion; the letter itself says scope and notification remain unknown |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k; DL 8) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Characterisation accepted without assessment |
| Tax/IP (Seller update) | Settled under general regime | Keep separate; no hidden general-regime override; open, no unlimited liability assumed | Pulls Tax/IP into the general regime |
| Title (DL 10; DD-012) | Share register at DD-012 evidences title | Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is internal, not independent | Seller's own register offered as proof |

## 3. Reasoning on the material issues

**a. Caps, basket and time limits.** Taken together, the Seller's package is materially weaker than our start point on every general-regime metric: a lower cap, a higher de minimis, a deductible basket five times ours, and a shorter claims period. The AUD 250k deductible basket alone means the Buyer bears the first AUD 250k of any warranty loss. Our starting position should be restored and none of these should be conceded in the mark-up.

**b. Fundamental and fraud protections.** These are the most serious departures. Putting title and capacity under the general regime, and applying exclusive-remedy and non-reliance language to all claims, would allow the Seller to limit recovery for title defects and deliberate misconduct. The playbook says fraud carve-outs cannot be waived. We should delete the Seller's "all Claims" wording and insert the fraud carve-out in each of cl 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5.

**c. Knowledge and disclosure.** The Seller's combination of whole-data-room disclosure (DL 1.1, 1.2) and a buyer-knowledge bar (cl 8.3) would shift the risk of every disclosed fact to the Buyer. Because the data room is large and indexed by reference, this is effectively a general disclosure with a constructive-knowledge defence. We should require specific disclosure against specific warranties and reject deemed disclosure.

**d. Bluefen.** Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue. The Seller proposes reasonable endeavours and treats consent as satisfied on delivery, while its own letter confirms no final consent or condition evidence is in the room. We should require an effective consent and evidence that all conditions in clauses 11.2 and 11.3 are satisfied before Completion, with consent as a condition precedent.

**e. Riverlark.** The facility is about AUD 3.2M and unpaid. Deferring the release until after Completion leaves the Buyer exposed to the Seller's lender and the security over the Company's assets. Repayment should come directly from the Completion funds with effective releases. Any post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.

**f. Bonuses and funds flow.** AUD 420k in conditional Completion bonuses is excluded from the draft funds flow, and the Seller says the amount is "a matter for the Seller". If the Company pays these after Completion, the cost falls on the Buyer. Either the amount is a specific funds-flow line, or it is seller-funded. On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) are unquantified and must be added to the figure.

**g. Ironquay IP.** The indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment, while DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 materials on payment of every SOW3 fee. The AUD 180k open amount is a Seller-supplied record, not bank verification of non-payment. We should broaden the indemnity to IP ownership and transfer defects, preserve the SOW3 cure, and require independent evidence of payment status.

**h. DD-006 export incident.** The letter describes about 1,240 records containing names, business emails, roles and activity timestamps, sent to an unintended external address, with scope, access and notification all unknown. The Seller's "not expected to be material" is a conclusion, not a finding. Under the playbook we assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantum either way. We should require preservation of logs, a completed investigation, and regular written updates. We should not put a number in the mark-up.

**i. Sandbar, Mossvale, office lease.** Sandbar's "ordinary course" label is unsupported. We should require an assessment of whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable or accrued, without treating it as Debt or deducting from price. Mossvale and the lease notification should be assessed for whether any consent is required on a share sale, rather than accepting "not required" from the Seller.

**j. Title.** DD-012 is the Company's own register, supplied by the Seller. It is useful but not independent proof. We should require independent evidence: an ASIC company extract, a share-transfer history, a search for encumbrances over the shares, and confirmation of authority.

**k. Tax and IP.** The Seller wants these to sit under the general regime. The playbook keeps them separate and open, without unlimited liability and without assuming resolution. We should reject the merger and mark both as open items.

## 4. Recommendations

1. **Cover note:** State that the Seller's FINAL labels, market-standard claims and "settled" language are not accepted. The Buyer's positions remain open until confirmed through its own authority process.
2. **Restore general regime:** Cap 25% / AUD 6.0M; de minimis AUD 5,000; first-dollar basket AUD 50,000; 24-month claims period. Do not offer the 20% / 18-month fallback without Amelia Frost's written authority.
3. **Separate Fundamental/Title:** 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. **Fraud carve-out:** Insert in cl 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5, and in all caps, baskets and time limits.
5. **Disclosure:** Specific fair disclosure only. Reject data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
6. **Knowledge:** Delete cl 8.3. Any replacement qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and must not excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Bluefen:** Effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions before Completion, as a condition precedent.
8. **Riverlark:** Payout from Completion funds, effective releases, and an irrevocable undertaking plus Frost approval for any post-completion release.
9. **Bonuses:** Add AUD 420k plus triggered on-costs as a funds-flow line, or make it seller-funded. Require on-cost calculation.
10. **Ironquay:** Broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and require independent payment verification.
11. **DD-006:** Require log preservation, investigation and updates. Accept no conclusion on materiality and no numeric demand.
12. **Sandbar, Mossvale, lease:** Require assessment. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
13. **Title:** Require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence. Treat DD-012 as internal only.
14. **Tax and IP:** Keep separate and open. Reject folding them into the general regime.
15. **Refresh:** Update all facts from the 22 September 2026 record before issuing the mark-up.
